clue.text: Pass over some money to workers?

parts.note: change is a quantity of coins, a little money
hands are manual workers, as in farmhands or all hands on deck

explanation.surface: A question about paying out cash to a workforce.
explanation.definitionFit: When property changes owner it is said to be passed over from one person to another.

clue.text: His Excellency with press chief pay attention

parts.note: HE is the standard abbreviation for His Excellency, an ambassador's title
the chief of a newspaper is its editor, abbreviated ED

explanation.surface: An ambassador and a newspaper editor are told to listen carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: To take notice of advice is to pay attention to it; a synonym.

clue.text: Duck on eastern river

parts.note: in cricket a duck is a score of zero, so nil

explanation.surface: A duck swimming on a river in the east.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck in cricket is a batsman's score of nought.
explanation.definitionFit: The great African waterway, an example of a river.

clue.text: Forming a unit in continental train

parts.note: the French word for in is en
a train is a retinue of attendants, also called a suite

explanation.surface: Something becoming part of a group aboard a train in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: French for 'in sequence', describing rooms or items that together form a set.

clue.text: One over 50 with just the thing that came down

indicators.note: in a down clue, one placed over another comes first, above it

parts.note: one is A, the indefinite article
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
it means exactly what is wanted, as in 'that's it'

explanation.surface: Someone past fifty with the perfect object that fell.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of the verb meaning to land or descend, as a bird settling.

clue.text: Lined up in uniform

definitions.meaning: soldiers dress their ranks when they straighten the line

explanation.definitionFit: Military parlance for aligning ranks, and also simply clothed or attired, as in uniform.

clue.text: Be concerned enough to wear a glove?

definitions.meaning: to be involved in or take part in something
a glove is literally worn by putting a palm inside it

explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for being involved in some matter; and, playfully, literally placing a palm within a glove.

clue.text: Underrating need for feather-sorting?

parts.note: down is soft fine plumage
grading is sorting by quality or size

explanation.surface: Asks whether undervaluing something is needed for classifying plumage.
explanation.definitionFit: Demoting or reducing in rank or value, close in sense to undervaluing.

clue.text: There's nothing after the end of month in Ireland

indicators.note: the round letter for nothing comes after the month's name

parts.note: May is a month of the year
O resembles zero, so nothing

explanation.surface: Something that happens at the end of a month in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: MAYO is an Irish county, so the definition is a place in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A county on the west coast of the Irish republic, a place located there.

clue.text: Look very happy-totally radiant?

definitions.meaning: being entirely made of beams and grins, glowing all over

explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for grinning broadly; and the whole face beaming, radiant through and through.

clue.text: Give baby a new concoction

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture made up, so these letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Feeding an infant a freshly mixed formula.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concoction' is the anagram signal, rearranging A NEW.
explanation.definitionFit: To accustom an infant to solid food instead of milk, giving it new fare.

clue.text: How a carpet manufacturer is amassing a fortune?

definitions.meaning: a carpet maker produces the raised tufts of a rug, its pile
becoming very rich, piling up money

explanation.definitionFit: A pile is a carpet's tufted surface, so a rug maker literally produces it; idiomatically it means getting wealthy.

clue.text: This medicine not being the first choice?

definitions.text: This medicine not being the first choice?

parts.words: This medicine not being the first choice?
parts.note: complementary therapies outside mainstream practice; also something chosen as a second option rather than the first

explanation.definitionFit: Complementary medicine is called by this name, and a second option is also so called.

clue.text: Greek maiden dropped second article in US city

indicators.note: dropped means the named letter is taken out of the maiden's name

parts.note: Atalanta was the swift huntress of Greek myth
a is the indefinite article; here its second appearance in her name

explanation.surface: A girl from Greek legend shed something in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the second A from ATALANTA leaves the Georgia capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Georgia, a major city in the United States.

clue.text: Sailor on edge completely full

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: A seaman perched on the brink, filled to the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Filled right up to the top, as a glass to its lip.

clue.text: Get to know about the moorland shrub

indicators.note: about means the first word goes round the other

parts.note: to hear of something is to learn about it

explanation.surface: Learning about the bushes that grow on the moors.
explanation.definitionFit: A low purple-flowered plant, typical of upland heath, also called ling.

clue.text: A row of boxes perhaps?

parts.note: box is an evergreen shrub; plants of it set in a line form a garden boundary

explanation.definitionFit: Box shrubs planted in a line make a garden boundary of this kind.

clue.text: Be returning to one's resting-place, having gone down

indicators.note: returning means the word Be is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a bed is where one rests

explanation.surface: Someone going back to bed after coming down.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of a tide's retreat, receded or declined.

clue.text: Cockney conceals date in March

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker drops the aitch at the start of words

parts.note: hides means conceals

explanation.surface: A London East Ender hiding a March appointment.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys are Londoners whose accent famously drops H, so HIDES becomes 'IDES.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Roman calendar the fifteenth of the third month was so named.

clue.text: Conclusion about island lady

indicators.note: about means the first word goes round the other

parts.note: an end is a conclusion

explanation.surface: An ending set around an island woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, so an example of a lady.

clue.text: House call

definitions.meaning: house is another name for the numbers game, from the shout of a full card
the cry a winner shouts out

explanation.definitionFit: The numbers game is also called house, and its name is what a winning player shouts.

clue.text: A poor actor among the graduates in the islands

indicators.note: among means set inside the other piece

parts.note: BA is Bachelor of Arts, so graduates are BAs
a ham is a bad overacting performer

explanation.surface: A bad performer mingling with university graduates in a tropical archipelago.
explanation.definitionFit: An Atlantic archipelago nation, a group of islands.

clue.text: Drove round the bend, having little energy as it's late

indicators.note: turned round, so the letters of the word drove are reordered

parts.note: a U-bend is a curve, so bend gives U
E is the abbreviation for energy

explanation.surface: A driver going crazy and tired because of lateness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round the bend' pretends to mean mad, but 'round' is the anagram signal and 'the bend' is a U-bend, a plumbing curve.
explanation.definitionFit: Past the expected time, tardy.

clue.text: Encouraging Hamish inside to have some cotton cloth

indicators.note: inside means the letters sit within the words Encouraging Hamish

explanation.surface: Persuading a Scot named Hamish to buy some fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A checked woven fabric, typically of cotton.

clue.text: Excuse found on vase I smashed

indicators.note: smashed means broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone finding an excuse after breaking a vase.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodging a question with an alibi; a pretext or excuse.

clue.text: Penny tucked into food

parts.note: to tuck into is to eat heartily, so ate

explanation.surface: A coin pushed inside a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked into' looks like a container signal but means ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A savoury paste, an example of food.

clue.text: Almost cheat lady from Germany…

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is missing

parts.note: a fraud is a cheat

explanation.surface: A German woman who is nearly a con artist.
explanation.definitionFit: German for wife or Mrs, a German woman.

clue.text: … soon getting a refusal from France

parts.note: non is French for no

explanation.surface: Shortly hearing a no from a French speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic word meaning shortly or presently.

clue.text: Sullen learner in sticky surroundings

indicators.note: in means the letter sits inside the gum

parts.note: gum is a sticky substance, here surrounding
L is for learner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: A grumpy student stuck in glue.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloomy or morose, close in sense to sulky.

clue.text: Insolently crossing river in a rash way

indicators.note: crossing means the word for insolently straddles the river letter

parts.note: impudently means insolently

explanation.surface: Someone rudely and rashly fording a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwisely or recklessly, acting rashly.

clue.text: Richard the poet didn't have lace — nothing

indicators.note: didn't have means the following letters are missing from his surname

parts.note: Richard Lovelace was a seventeenth-century English Cavalier poet

explanation.surface: A poet named Richard who had no lace trimming.
explanation.walkthrough: Lovelace wrote 'To Althea, from Prison'; in tennis scoring the word means zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Zero in tennis scoring, so nothing.

clue.text: Pretended to call an alias

parts.note: assumed means feigned or pretended
to name is to call

explanation.surface: Someone feigning to address another by a false name.
explanation.definitionFit: A false identity taken on, a synonym for pseudonym.
